STLA.role: Five regional vehicle businesses; financial operations separately reported.
STLA.financial_mechanism: Vehicle replacement, a better product range and reduced factory underutilization could restore ordinary cash margins, without a return to2023 record profitability.
STLA.reason: Corrected DCF base $7.25 / weighted $7.72; serious turnaround risk. Fails extreme-gap hurdle after cash research spending and replacement investment are aligned. Combined stress is zero; hybrids, pension claims and operating cash reserve deducted.

DINO.role: Refineries, renewable diesel, marketing, lubricants and midstream assets.
DINO.financial_mechanism: Regional supply closures and distribution advantages can improve refining and lubricant margins.
DINO.reason: Q2 refining margin of $25.95/barrel and lubricant FIFO gains were unusually favorable. Current price requires normalized cash flow analysis; one-quarter annualization is insufficient. Not advanced, rather than proven overvalued.

HUN.role: Polyurethanes, performance products and advanced materials manufacturing.
HUN.financial_mechanism: Construction and insulation recovery can improve plant utilization and cash margins.
HUN.reason: The signed all-stock Olin merger changes the security being purchased. A standalone model would misstate future economics; the combined merger valuation remains unresolved. Q2 free cash outflow was $90m.

CE.role: Acetyl chemicals and qualified engineering polymers.
CE.financial_mechanism: Low-cost Western plants and better medical/electronics product mix can improve cash generation.
CE.reason: Management expects temporary supply opportunities to normalize, while raw-material costs catch up. $12.007bn debt puts creditors ahead of common shareholders. A full cycle and liability model is unresolved.

ASIX.role: Integrated cumene-to-phenol/acetone, caprolactam and nylon production, with ammonium sulfate coproduct.
ASIX.financial_mechanism: Lower project spending and more granular nutrient output could increase cash conversion.
ASIX.reason: Detailed DCF rejects the stock: $12.04 base and $12.94 weighted value versus $17.37. Even a 6% normalized EBIT margin fails to support the price after capital spending. Nylon oversupply and October2027 refinancing remain material.

SBSW.role: South African platinum-group-metals and gold mining, US PGM mining and recycling.
SBSW.financial_mechanism: Mine closures and cost discipline can strengthen commodity prices and operating cash margins.
SBSW.reason: H1 earnings rebounded with metal prices and a ZAR9.361bn working-capital benefit. Published net debt excludes Burnstone. ADR, convertible dilution and full mining liability bridges remain unresolved.

VALE.role: Iron ore, copper and nickel mines supported by logistics infrastructure.
VALE.financial_mechanism: Low-cost ore output and copper projects could support cash generation despite lower ore premiums.
VALE.reason: Its own Serra Sul expansion adds20Mt of annual ore capacity. Q2 copper prices were already $14,062/t, while expanded net debt was $16.677bn. Supply normalization and liability modeling are still required.

EC.role: Oil and gas production, refining, transport and ISA electricity transmission.
EC.financial_mechanism: Refinery utilization and regulated infrastructure can diversify cash generation across the oil cycle.
EC.reason: Record refining margins of $29.8/barrel are cyclical. Natural upstream decline around18% requires replacement investment; COP8tn FEPC receivables lock up cash. Acquisition and political claims remain unresolved.

PBR.role: Brazilian pre-salt oil production, refining and transport.
PBR.financial_mechanism: Low lifting costs and new offshore platforms can increase output and cash flow.
PBR.reason: Q2 Brent averaged $104.52/barrel and reported free cash flow excludes lease principal. Net debt of $60.388bn includes leased platforms. No complete normalized reserve and decommissioning valuation was established.

MEOH.role: Global methanol production and distribution, including partially owned plants.
MEOH.financial_mechanism: Gas-constrained shutdowns can improve margins for low-cost North American supply.
MEOH.reason: Q2 realized price of $529/t versus $351/t in Q1 already captures disruption. The September1 announcement sells New Zealand gas entitlements and idles production from2027, transferring some value away from manufacturing. Peak spreads are not sustainable valuation inputs.

MOS.role: Phosphate and potash mining, fertilizer production and Brazilian distribution.
MOS.financial_mechanism: Lower sulfur costs could restore phosphate margins and cash conversion.
MOS.reason: The current bottleneck hurts cash: Q3 sulfur contracts were $705/long ton and Q2 operating loss was $36m. $1.2bn capital spending and Brazilian curtailments constrain near-term cash. The Maaden investment needs separate valuation.
